components.note: 王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.
心 (heart/mind) — 想 relates to thinking, missing someone, or wanting something in one's heart.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — 想 is pronounced xiǎng, matching aside from tone.
辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
攵 (to act, strike) — 敏 describes being quick and effective in action, 'nimble, sharp.'
每 (měi) is only distantly related in sound to mǐn — the rhyme has drifted apart over time.
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
禾 (grain, a rice/wheat plant) — 科 relates to sorting and measuring crops.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring grain into ordered categories gave 科 its meaning 'a branch of study' or 'a department.'
扌 (hand) — relates to 技's meaning 'skill, technique,' a skill performed with the hands.
支 (zhī) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jì.
勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'
衣 (clothes) — 裹 relates to wrapping something, like fabric around an object.
果 (guǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 裹.
工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.
贝 (shell/money) — 资 relates to wealth, funds, and resources.
次 (cì) gives a hint of the sound — 资 is pronounced zī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'

女 (woman) forms the left side of the character.
彐 depicts a broom — a woman holding a broom, a traditional image of housework, gave 妇 its meaning 'married woman, wife.'
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
氵 (water) — 源 originally referred to the spring where a river begins
原 (yuán) gives the sound — an exact match with 源's reading yuán
刂 (knife) — 判 originally related to cutting something apart to distinguish or decide
半 (bàn) gives a sound close to 判's reading pàn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.
纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
毛 (fur/hair) — 毯 names a woven covering made from fur or wool.
炎 (yán) gives a sound distantly related to tǎn, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — 依 relates to a person relying or leaning on something
衣 (yī) gives the sound — 依 is also pronounced yī, an exact match
非 (two things back-to-back) — 靠 relates to leaning against or relying on something
告 (gào) gives a sound distantly related to 靠's reading kào, having drifted apart over time
扌 (hand) — throwing is an action done with the hand.
乃 (nǎi) gives a sound distantly related to rēng, having drifted apart over time.
扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.
衤 (clothes) — 裸 describes the absence of clothing, being bare.
果 (guǒ) gives a sound close to luǒ, sharing the same rhyme.
阝 (a mound, related to terrain) — the ground where something happens.
臽 (a pit) — a hole in the ground, together giving 陷 its meaning 'to sink, to fall into a trap.'
On the left side, 阝 derives from 阜 (mound, earthworks), pointing to something dug into the ground.
井 means 'well' and is pronounced jǐng — the same as 阱 — evoking a deep pit dug into the earth like a well, which gave 阱 its meaning 'pitfall, trap.'
八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'
口 (mouths) — 总 pictures many voices.
心 (heart, mind) — many mouths brought together under one mind gave 总 its meaning 'overall' or 'to gather together.'
⺮ (bamboo) — the material of ancient counting rods.
具 (held in two hands) — bamboo counting rods or an abacus held up for use, the tools of calculation that gave 算 its meaning 'to calculate, count.'
直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

meanings: auxiliary showing sth happened in the past

components.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
十 (ten) — suggests something repeated many times.
口 (mouth) — a story passed down through ten generations of mouths gave 古 its meaning 'old, ancient.'
耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.

meanings: (of a turn of events) not too encouraging

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
女 (woman) — 妙 originally described a young woman's delicate charm, extended to mean 'wonderful, clever.'
少 (shǎo) gives a sound distantly related to miào, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) shows 伪 describes something false or counterfeit, often about people's actions or claims.
为 (wéi) gives a sound very close to wěi, differing mainly in tone.
衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match
宀 (roof) marks the setting — a house or hall.
妟 (a woman 女 beneath the sun 日) suggests ease and comfort — people gathered comfortably under a roof, giving 宴 its meaning 'banquet, feast.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
扌 (hand) — a hand held out, palm up
乇 — something resting on the upturned palm for support
Originally depicted a burning candle or the sun's rays radiating outward — the source of 白's meaning 'white, bright, clear.'
宀 (roof) — 宫 names a palace, a grand building.
吕 (lǚ) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading gōng has diverged considerably.

meanings: to issue (an official document or credential)

components.note: 关 — a person's arms shown in a waving or embracing gesture, bidding farewell
辶 (to walk) — the person walking away who is being seen off
冫 (water/ice) — 冲 relates to liquid, as in pouring or rinsing with water
中 (zhōng) gives a sound close to 冲's reading chōng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
穴 (a cave/hole) — the den the dog bursts from.
犬 (dog) — a dog suddenly darting out of its den gave 突 its meaning 'sudden, abrupt.'
扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
A pictograph of an altar or offering table used in ancestor worship — presenting offerings extended to 示's meaning 'to show, display, indicate.'

meanings: to have no other option but to ...

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the source of speech.
八 here suggests something small or simple leaving the mouth, giving 只 its meaning 'only, merely.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
散 traditionally depicts a hand (攵) scattering something, like seeds tossed from a basket — the image behind its meaning 'to scatter, disperse.'
止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'
女 (woman) — 妆 describes putting on makeup, an action tied to appearance.
丬 gives a sound related to zhuāng, though the connection has drifted apart over time.
另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.
扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
刂 (knife) contributes to the character's form, though its link to 剧's meaning 'drama' has faded over time.
居 (jū) gives a rhyme close to jù, with the tone shifted.
阝 (a mound/enclosure) — relates to 院's meaning 'courtyard, institution,' an enclosed place.
完 (wán) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from yuàn.
卑 traditionally pictures a hand holding an empty, lowly object — an old image behind its meaning 'low, humble.'
阝 (village) — an older semantic link to a remote, rustic place, hence 鄙's sense of "low, base."
啚 (bǐ) gives the sound — an exact match with 鄙.
忄 (heart) — 怀 relates to feelings held close to the heart
不 (bù) gives a sound distantly related to 怀's reading huái, having drifted apart over time
今 (now, the present) — represents what is currently on one's mind.
心 (heart/mind) — keeping the present moment in mind gave 念 its meaning 'to think of, to read aloud, to study.'
宀 (roof) — 宽 originally described a spacious house.
苋 (xiàn) gives a sound distantly related to kuān, having drifted apart over time.
心 (heart) — 恕 describes a heartfelt willingness to forgive.
如 (rú) gives a sound only distantly related to shù today, having drifted apart over time.
厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 原 relates to a source high up, such as a spring emerging from rock.
泉 (quán) gives a hint of the sound — 原 is pronounced yuán, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'

meanings: to gain first-hand knowledge of sth

components.note: 冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'
讠 (speech) — relates to 识's meaning 'to know, recognize,' knowledge conveyed through words.
只 (zhǐ) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shí.
户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'

夫 (man) is shown twice, side by side, one man standing in for another.
日 sits below, together giving 替 its meaning 'to replace, to substitute.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
A pictograph of an ancient forked weapon, such as a club or shield-tipped spear — the tool image later extended to 干's meanings 'to do, to work' and, in another reading, 'dry.'
⺼ (flesh) — 脆 originally described flesh that tears or breaks easily.

弓 here pictures a young, bent shoot rather than a bow.

水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.
田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
尺 (a ruler/measure) — represents rules or measures being set.
口 (mouth) — measures being discussed aloud in one place gave 局 its meaning 'bureau, office, situation.'
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.
